name: Black Systems Solar

pitch_detail.notes: First pitch on lower west-facing wall section
Second pitch with mid-route anchor to upper anchors

descent_text: A 70m rope will not reach the ground when lowering from the top anchors — descend via the mid-height anchor in two stages, or simply lower each pitch in turn if climbing it as two pitches.
approach: From Seattle, drive east on I-90 to Snoqualmie Pass and take Exit 54, crossing to the north side of the freeway before turning onto FR 4832, then following it onto FR 4934 to the small trailhead pullout. On foot, cross the road and hike up a spur road for about 15 minutes to a flat bench, then pick up a cairned trail heading north into the forest to a rocky area, staying on the main climber's trail through a short, steeper forest section to reach the crag — roughly 25-30 minutes total from the car. A Northwest Forest Pass is generally expected for parking at national forest trailheads in this corridor.
overview: 5.9 sport route on Keechelus Ridge, featuring accessible climbing with excellent views and described as one of the best 5.9s in Washington.
beta: Two-pitch sport climb on a lower west-facing wall section of Keechelus Ridge. Can be climbed as one continuous pitch or split into two pitches using mid-route anchors. Described as one of the best 5.9s in Washington with commanding views from the belay stations. Belay ledge provides excellent sun protection during morning and midday hours.
